sentences.text:
Heard Sri Rahul Dev Singh, Advocate holding brief of Sri Zafar Abbas, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Ms. Ifrah Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.139 of 2024, under Sections 363, 376, 506, 343 I.P.C.,
Police Station- Azeemnagar, District- Rampur, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
3. The applicant is stated to have enticed away the daughter of the informant on 9.5.2024 and had raped her several times and left her on 12.5.2024.
The victim was found keeping mum in the house for several days.

After delving deep and questioning her, she is stated to have revealed the incident Arman vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32073575/
1
to the members of the family, as such the FIR was instituted on 24.5.2024.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
4. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
5. The FIR is delayed by about twelve days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Rather the FIR may be termed as delayed by about fifteen days from the date when the victim was found missing from the house.
6. The prosecution story itself seems improbable as narrated in the FIR as it is nowhere mentioned that they had questioned the victim about her absence for about three days.
7. The victim is a consenting party as is but evident from the circumstances and her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
Although, it has been mentioned that applicant had committed rape with her.

8. The age of the victim has deliberately been suppressed by the prosecution as the victim told her age to be 13 years, but as per the school certificate of Class-8th her date of birth is stated to be 4.4.2005, as such she was more than 19 years old at the time of offence.
By her physical appearance also, the victim seems to be major.
9. The allegations under Section 3/4 POCSO Act have been deleted by the Investigating Officer and the final report (charge-sheet) has been filed under Sections 363, 376, 506, 343 I.P.C. only.
10. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
11. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 3.6.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/OPPOSITE PARTY 12.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:
13. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

Arman vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32073575/
2 14.

A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
15.

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
16. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
17. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant- Arman involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
20. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

21. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the Arman vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32073575/
